EUR.catalyst: The euro remains subdued against major peers following the European Central Bank's September policy meeting, where officials delivered a expected 25-basis-point interest rate increase to take the benchmark rate to 2.65%. Market participants view the ECB's tightening capacity as increasingly constrained by fragile Eurozone growth dynamics alongside elevated crude oil and natural gas prices. Central bank officials have highlighted these energy cost pressures, with Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel noting that "recent energy-price developments have been quite concerning," while Governing Council members Yannis Stournaras and Peter Kazimir signaled that all options remain open for future policy moves. Against the greenback, the single currency trades below its 20-day (1.1630) and 200-day (1.1637) simple moving averages while holding just above its 50-day SMA benchmark at 1.1532.
